definition: Intelligent control is a class of control techniques that use various artificial intelligence computing approaches like neural networks, Bayesian probability, fuzzy logic, machine learning, reinforcement learning, evolutionary computation and genetic algorithms..
details: Intelligent control is a class of control techniques that use various artificial intelligence computing approaches like neural networks, Bayesian probability, fuzzy logic, machine learning, reinforcement learning, evolutionary computation and genetic algorithms.

explainer.lead: Intelligent control is a class of control techniques that apply AI computing approaches to controlling systems. It matters because it brings learning and probabilistic methods into control rather than relying only on conventional techniques.

tiers.eli5: Instead of a fixed set of rules for steering a machine, the controller uses learning-style methods to decide what to do.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers draw on neural networks, fuzzy logic, reinforcement learning, Bayesian probability, evolutionary computation and genetic algorithms; a pitfall is picking an AI method whose behavior is hard to verify in a safety-critical loop.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as a class of control techniques using AI computing approaches such as neural networks, Bayesian probability, fuzzy logic, machine learning, reinforcement learning, evolutionary computation and genetic algorithms.

explainer.example: A controller tuned with reinforcement learning adjusts a system's actions based on feedback rather than a hand-coded rule set.
